sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Onboarding for synthetic users: invented personas, a sub-agent each, a real browser, one vault, published anywhere.
sections.para: A Claude session reads a vault of invented personas, each with a role, personality, direction of travel and mission, and starts one sub-agent per persona to drive a real browser one screenshot at a time, recording questions and confusion, then interviews them and maps the findings. Not user research, but three runs found what tests missed. Start with a key from sgraph.ai or from Dinis, sgit, a vault, and a read key to publish.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: The question, the method, the screenshot rule, one vault, three runs, how to start and how to publish.
sections.para: The vault key stays private; the read key is what you publish and embed.

sections.label: The question
sections.line: What does the site look like to an executive, a security specialist, a business owner and a founder?
sections.para: Ask real people too; invented ones are cheap and available today, if you are honest about what they are.

sections.label: What it is, and what it is not
sections.line: Everyone in it is invented; it is not user research. The browser's record is the evidence.
sections.para: Good at finding where a page loses someone; poor at saying how many real people it would lose.

sections.label: What it has found
sections.line: Three runs: store.sgit.ai, riskmandate.ai and the newsroom, each finding things no test had.
sections.para: A buyer on a phone, a product not named where it was sold, a JavaScript error on every page, no contact for a pilot, 51 missing figures.

sections.label: How it works
sections.line: A vault of personas, one Claude session, one sub-agent per persona, a seven-step loop on screenshots.
sections.para: Each persona has a role, personality, direction of travel, device and mission; agents never read the page's code, so they can get lost like a person; then an interview and a map of findings.

sections.label: What goes in the vault
sections.line: Personas, expected journeys, the protocol, checks, runs, tools and an app, all in the vault.
sections.para: Writing the journeys first shows where reality differed; the protocol in the vault makes the next run comparable.

sections.label: Getting started
sections.line: Get a key, install sgit, create the vault, keep the vault key safe, run, publish.

sections.label: What I would tell you before your first run
sections.line: Pick personas who disagree, write journeys first, put one on a phone, keep the failures, run again.
sections.para: A run with no confusion was not done properly.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Not user research; findings as the vaults report them; the key and server will change.
sections.para: The prompt shown is a starting point, not the one behind the published runs.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Dinis's conversation, the three study vaults, sgit-ai 0.27.0, sgraph.ai's pricing page and this site's embed script.
